question: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait it is observed that:

options.opa: The trait appears more frequently in males.
options.opb: The unaffected people do not transmit the trait.
options.opc: The trait tends to skip generations.
options.opd: The affected people have both affected parents.
options.ope: The trait tends to appear in the progeny of related parents.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait typically appears in every generation" -> "unaffected individuals do not transmit the trait" -> "confirms option opb" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait can be passed from affected parent to child" -> "trait does not skip generations" -> "conflicts with option opc" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait can appear in both males and females" -> "no gender bias in transmission" -> "conflicts with option opa" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "affected individuals can have affected or unaffected parents" -> "does not confirm option opd" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "inbreeding increases chances of trait expression" -> "may support option ope" -> 75%
analysis: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait, it is observed that unaffected individuals do not transmit the trait, as the trait requires at least one affected allele to be passed on. This means that option 'opb' is correct. The other options do not accurately describe the inheritance pattern of autosomal dominant traits.
